lines: The best wall is boring. Boring means it held.
One bad chip once made me redo a whole doorway. It was right to complain.
An arch looks impossible until the last stone <bold>proves everyone wrong</bold>.
There is a story from the stonecutter, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Most stories here begin with someone saying, 'It will only take a moment.' They are always wrong.
I remember the smell of rain, the sound of the bell, and everyone suddenly pretending they had a plan.
The funny part came later. At the time, nobody was laughing.
A village story changes depending on who got embarrassed in it.
I could make it grand, but honestly, it was mostly mud, noise, and bad timing.
Still, we tell it because we made it through, and that makes people stand a little straighter.
Once a wall leaned for three days out of spite before we rebuilt it.
A child stacked pebbles beside my work and called it a tower. Ambitious critic.
I found an old mark in a foundation and wondered who trusted it first.
During one storm, the chimney held and everyone suddenly respected boring work.
A trader asked if stone could be lighter. I asked if gravity could be kinder.
The first arch I made stood long enough for me to stop holding my breath.
A stair I repaired stopped three people from blaming their own feet.
There was a week when every corner in the village needed an opinion.
I once carved a name wrong and learned humility with a chisel.
A golem watched me work on a wall and made me feel very supervised.
The oldest doorstep here is worn smooth by more stories than I can count.
A chimney once smoked backward and turned breakfast into a mystery.
I hauled stone through mud and discovered new ways to dislike mud.
One cracked pillar taught five villagers the value of moving quickly.
I built a small wall for a garden and it became a favorite sitting place.
